drafts.label: Project Description
drafts.answer:
E2A2O is a conversation-led workspace for someone with more ideas than time to coordinate them. Think out loud. Keep your place. Speak or type, move between topics, and return to an unfinished thought.

We are extending that base into a way to build software through conversation: Muse Spark works on small, reusable parts in separate Git branches while the person keeps shaping the goal. The intended workflow checks each part, combines working changes, and repairs or switches off failed parts without losing the rest. Parts can be made from smaller parts and reused in later work.

The current prototype has a Rust core, a TypeScript interface, topic organization, return-to-thought navigation and bounded Spark coding proposals in isolated worktrees. The complete speech-to-parallel-build-to-checked-merge-and-repair loop still needs an end-to-end demonstration; we do not claim it is finished. A labelled sample works without an AI key; live model features need a Meta key.

Before the event there were ideas and design notes, no app code. Original app code was written during the event; third-party dependencies retain their licences.

drafts.label: Describe your use of Meta products to build the submitted project
drafts.answer:
Muse Voice Transcribe turns spoken input into text. Muse Spark organizes thoughts by topic, supports refinement and Recap, and produces bounded coding proposals for isolated worktrees. Our intended extension uses Spark to divide a request into reusable parts, build them concurrently and repair failed checks; the complete integration loop remains to be demonstrated. Muse Image generates topic pictures for the optional visual view.

During development, Muse Code with Muse Wonder Full reviewed supplied source snapshots. That was a development review, not a runtime component or proof that its recommendations were implemented. The app's live model functions use Meta models; ordinary code handles storage, navigation, branch isolation and checks.

drafts.label: Why are Meta's models important to your solution?
drafts.answer: Meta's models connect a spoken intention to work the person can inspect. Voice Transcribe makes speech usable as input. Spark interprets the meaning of a thought, organizes it and produces a scoped code proposal instead of requiring a person to translate every idea into a detailed task. The intended parallel-parts workflow builds on those proposals, with ordinary code enforcing boundaries and checks. Muse Image adds an optional visual way to revisit topics. These roles let us explore whether someone can keep thinking while the workspace carries work forward. We have not established a productivity or reliability improvement.
